text:
anna: Heads-up. Observed a customer app hit duplicate side-effects when gateway retried streaming requests after idle conn drop. Repro: long-lived stream, client idle ~30s, NAT timeout, reconnect -> gateway treats previous stream as failed -> hedges -> duplicate call. Anyone seen this? :thinking:

devin: yep. NAT/timeouts + proxy keepalive mismatch is classic. We currently treat stream termination vs connection loss differently for retry budget. Edge sees TCP FIN vs abrupt close and may trigger soft-hedge.

sanjay: do we have an idempotency header for streaming workflows? For unary we use `x-rw-idempotency-key` but streams don't carry a single logical op.

anna: right. For some streaming RPCs we support resume tokens, but those are app-level (model KV). Gateway can't assume resume semantics.

maria: quick thought: add a connection-liveliness marker that proxies upstream can attach so downstream can detect whether client reconnected vs stream aborted. e.g., `x-rw-conn-id` + `x-rw-conn-seq`? Would help correlate reconnections.

devin: +1. If gateway can tag `x-rw-conn-id` and treat reconnect within TTL as "client resumed" rather than "previous stream failed" we can avoid hedging fallbacks. TTL configurable per route.

anna: tradeoffs: requires client to echo conn-id on reconnect or gateway store short-lived session. Which do we prefer?

sanjay: storing ephemeral session state at edge breaks statelessness, but it's probably limited scope and TTL. Could also make clients responsible: they send `x-rw-conn-id` on reconnect and we match by that header.

maria: clients won't change overnight. We should design both: accept client-supplied conn-id and fallback to ephemeral keep-in-memory for same-source IP + auth tie if present.

devin: also need to align keepalive vs hedging timers. Proposal:

```
route:
  stream_reconnect_ttl_ms: 45000
  hedge_delay_ms: 1500
  conn_keepalive_interval_ms: 20000
  accept_resume_header: true
```

If reconnect happens within stream_reconnect_ttl we treat as resume — no hedging, forward data to resumed session (if resume token exists) else drop hedging and send soft-defer.

anna: what about side-effecting endpoints where resume is not possible? Should we enforce `x-rw-retry-mode` with values `none|idempotent|resume` and reject hedging if none?

sanjay: that helps. Gateway can require routes to declare retry-mode; default `idempotent` for unary, `resume` for streaming when backend supports it.

maria: observability: add metrics `edge.conn_resume_attempts`, `edge.conn_resume_success`, `edge.hedge_blocked_by_conn_resume`. Also log correlation id: `x-rw-trace` + `x-rw-conn-id` in traces/Spans.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for `edge/proxy@conn-resume-v1` on us-west-2 (3 nodes) :rocket: 

anna: action items:
- implement `x-rw-conn-id` support + accept client-echo on reconnect (devin)
- route config flags (sanjay)
- metrics & console surfaces (maria)
- docs + client hint (anna)

devin: i'll start a minimal PR for header handling in ingress pipeline and add unit tests for race where TCP reset precedes reconnect within TTL.

sanjay: will sketch route proto and default policy; also add check forbidding resume on routes with side-effects unless explicit `retry-mode: resume`.

maria: i'll wire metrics and add a Console card for per-route resume rate + blocked hedges.

anna: cool. ping me when PRs linked. Thanks all :thumbsup:
